features.method: Computed: station 11's published offsets (easting -1572.9 m, northing 730.0 m, pos_site 'summit') from the RNO_season_2022.json detector description were added to the published origin (72.582793 N, -38.455815 E, the DISC borehole) in a spherical local tangent plane (R = 6 371 008.8 m; dlat = N/R, dlon = E/(R cos 72.582793 deg)), giving 72.5893581 N, -38.5030726 E. The offsets are taken as true-east/true-north metres; if the collaboration's easting/northing axes are grid-aligned instead (UTM zone 24 convergence is about 0.5 degrees here), stations 4 km north of the origin would move by up to about 40 m, hence accuracy_m 100.

features.method: OpenStreetMap ways 1001537503-1001537513, eleven building=yes polygons with no name or other tag (all created 2021-11-11 and never edited), 0.15 to 1.0 km south of the DISC borehole, kept as eleven rings of one MultiPolygon with nodes unchanged. None is identified with a named building.
features.name: Summit Station camp area: eleven unnamed building footprints (OpenStreetMap)

provenance.locator: OSM ways 1001537503-1001537513, version 1, read from the OSM API 0.6 at 2026-10-25T11:10:31Z
provenance.note: OpenStreetMap alone; unnamed and untagged. The official page lists the Big House (26 ft x 56 ft), Green House/Berthing Module, Science and Operations Barn, Summit Mobile Garage (32 x 97 ft) and others, but no footprint's dimensions matches any of them within a few percent (best fit: the 30.2 x 11.8 m way 1001537504 against the Mobile Garage's 29.5 x 9.7 m), so none is named.
provenance.quote: The main station campus consists of the Big House, Green House/Berthing Module, and the Science and Operations Barn.

features.method: Published coordinate used verbatim: the RNO-G detector code returns (72.582793 N, -38.455815 E) as the position of the DISC borehole, 'used as the origin of the RNO-G coordinate system'. The RNO-G station paper's Figure 1 also marks a 'DISC Borehole' beside 'Big House' at that spot (viewed, not traced).
features.name: DISC borehole, the origin of the RNO-G coordinate system

provenance.note: 'verified': representation is 'surveyed' (a published coordinate) from a rank<=10 source. The coordinate is a software constant quoted to six decimals; its own survey is not published, so accuracy_m is set to 10 m.
provenance.quote: The returned location corresponds to the position of the DISC borehole which is used as the origin of the RNO-G coordinate system

features.method: OpenStreetMap way 704074469 (aeroway=runway, surface=ice), used verbatim as the skiway centre line; nodes kept as fetched, no simplification. Its measured length is checked against the 16,800 ft given on the station's own page.
features.name: Summit Station skiway (snow runway)

provenance.locator: OSM way 704074469 (version 2, last edited 2020-12-01T15:17:46Z), read from the OSM API 0.6 at 2026-10-25T11:10:31Z
provenance.note: Confidence 'verified' rests on the passing length check against the official GEOSummit page (a rank<=10 source); the centre line's width (200 ft officially) is not drawn.
provenance.quote: The skiway (snow runway) is 16,800 feet long and 200 feet wide.

map.name: Summit Station, Greenland — RNO-G stations, skiway and camp

summary.plain: Summit Station on top of the Greenland ice sheet, drawn to scale with its 5-kilometre skiway, the camp's building footprints and the seven RNO-G radio-neutrino stations installed in 2021 and 2022 on a grid about 1.25 kilometres apart.

unlocated.backlog: Georeference the official 'Summit Station Site Plan (2016)' or 'Summit Overall Site Plan and Skiway Layout (2014)' (linked from the Working at Summit page; cite, never copy) against the OSM skiway and the DISC borehole to name the buildings, or find a GEOSummit GIS layer; the 'Summit GIS' page on geo-summit.org was not reachable as a downloadable dataset.
unlocated.reason: Summit Station's named buildings: the Big House (26 ft x 56 ft), Green House/Berthing Module, Science and Operations Barn, Summit Mobile Garage (32 ft x 97 ft), Atmospheric Watch Observatory (150 sq ft, about 1 km south of the station) and Mobile Science Facility (16 ft x 36 ft). OpenStreetMap has eleven unnamed footprints near the camp (drawn as one context feature) but none can be matched to the official dimensions, and several of these buildings are moved on sleds.
